conv1.text: How are we looking on the September launch date?

conv2.text: Honestly, engineering is two weeks behind. The billing migration took longer than we expected.

conv3.text: Okay. What would it take to still hit the first week of September?

conv4.text: We would need to cut the analytics dashboard from version one and ship it in October.

conv5.text: I can live with that. Are there any risks with the app review process?

conv6.text: Maybe. I will confirm with the review team tomorrow and send you an update.

cut.text: Before we wrap up, the single most important action item is to send the revised contract to the partner by Friday.

hard1.text: Okay, quick sync before the board call. We only have ten minutes, so let's move fast. Where did the quarter three pricing experiment land?

hard2.text: Better than forecast. The annual tier converted at fourteen point two percent, up from eleven, but monthly churn crept to six point one percent.

hard4.text: The churn is concentrated in accounts we migrated off the legacy Postgres cluster, so I suspect the export tool, not the price.

hard5.text: Wait. The export tool, or the import wizard? Because Priya's team already patched the wizard on March third.

hard6.text: The export tool. Nguyen profiled it on Kubernetes and the batch jobs were timing out after ninety seconds.

hard8.text: So here is my proposal. We backport the fix, raise the timeout to three hundred seconds, rerun the SOC two evidence collection, and ship it behind a feature flag by Friday.

hard9.text: Hold on, hold on. Compliance needs two weeks notice for anything that touches audit evidence. Aisha was explicit about that.

hard10.text: Fair. Then we ship the timeout fix now and defer the evidence rerun to the April window.

hard11.text: Okay. What does that do to the forecast we are showing the board?

hard12.text: Honestly, revenue holds at roughly eight hundred twenty thousand for the quarter. The real risk is optics. The four enterprise renewals we are forwarding to legal could slip a week.

hard13.text: As long as it is not two of the four, we are fine. Anything else before I brief Marcus?

hard14.text: One more thing. The AppSumo cohort. Redemption is at sixty one percent, and the codes expire on the thirty first, so expect a support spike.

hard15.text: Good catch. Send me the churn breakdown by noon, and nice work on the profiling.

hard16.text: Will do. Talk after the board call.

long.text: Let me walk through the whole revenue model from the top because I think we keep talking past each other. The subscription tier brings in about forty thousand a month and it grows roughly five percent quarter over quarter. The marketplace side is lumpier because launches spike and then decay, but the baseline has been climbing steadily since February. If we combine both streams and subtract the partner payouts, the contribution margin lands somewhere around thirty eight percent. That number is the one I want everyone to remember, because every decision about discounts, about hiring, and about the September launch has to be justified against that margin, not against top line revenue, which is the mistake we made last year.
